newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal nears request to join WTO.
newsitem.headline: Nepal nears request to join WTO.

text.p: Nepal is close to completing a demand to join the World Trade Organization (WTO), officials said on Tuesday.
"We are at the last stage of finalizing our draft memorandum," Janak Raj Joshi, a senior Commerce Ministry official, told Reuters.

Currently, Nepal is an observer at the Geneva-based WTO. One of the 10 poorest nations, Nepal decided last year to join the WTO to benefit from concessions available to least developed member countries.
Nepal is not entitled to most favoured nation (MFN) status and national treatment in matters of trade unless it joins the WTO.

MFN is an undertaking by two countries to give each other the maximum tariff concessions on mutual trade which they already grant to other member countries. National treatment provides imported goods the same treatment as is given to domestic products.

Last July, the government set up an inter-ministerial committee to prepare for the accession process, which requires a country to provide details on its economy, trade, finance, investment measures and intellectual property protection.
The memorandum will be submitted soon to the WTO working party, but admission could then take more than a year, officials said.
